answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by stake and confiscates the bond when a randomly sampled task reveals fraud, so splitting one fortune across a tundra of aliases does not create free votes: each identity needs capital at risk. Honest agents can compare repeated claims across a knoll of tasks and share evidence through a grove of peers, making costly, coordinated deception easier to expose. The attacker pays in locked funds and expected slashing.
